title: What is the difference between String and StringBuilder?
description: Understand string immutability and when to use StringBuilder.

data.text: **Question:** What is the difference between String and StringBuilder?
String is immutable - every modification creates a new object in memory. StringBuilder is mutable and designed for efficient string manipulation, especially in loops.

**String:**
- Immutable: cannot be changed after creation
- Each concatenation creates a new string
- Stored in string intern pool
- Suitable for fixed strings or few operations
- Thread-safe by nature

**StringBuilder:**
- Mutable: can modify without creating new object
- Uses a character array internally
- Grows dynamically as needed
- Suitable for loops and many concatenations
- Not thread-safe

data.title: String vs StringBuilder

data.caption: String concatenation creates new objects each time; StringBuilder modifies a single reusable buffer in place.

data.text:
Interviewers want to assess:
- Understanding of immutability
- Knowledge of memory allocation
- Performance awareness
- When to choose each approach

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: String is fine for few operations
data.takeaway: Use StringBuilder in loops to avoid creating many temporary string objects.
